findings.title: Monad serves balances, call results and PoolManager receipts at latest from a proposed block that has no vote yet
findings.difference: Since v0.13.0 the Monad RPC maps latest to the Proposed state, a block the leader has sent and the node has executed speculatively before any quorum certificate exists. Ethereum's latest is a block that already carries proposer weight in the fork choice; Monad's latest has none. safe is Voted and finalized is Finalized.
findings.mechanism: monad-rpc v0.16.7 resolves BlockTags::Latest (and pending) to get_latest_proposed_block_key (monad-rpc/src/data/mod.rs:91-93 and 102-106, monad-rpc/src/types/eth_json.rs:328-330 and 373-376). eth_getTransactionReceipt first reads the in-memory buffer and then looks up the transaction location against the latest proposed block key (monad-rpc/src/data/mod.rs:196-225), so a receipt is served as soon as the proposed block is executed. A wallet, router or bridge that releases value on such a receipt, a Transfer log or a balance read at latest acts on a block that consensus can still abandon: a proposal that fails to collect a QC, or one of two blocks an equivocating leader sent, is dropped implicitly when another block finalizes at that height (docs.monad.xyz block states). The PoolManager itself is not affected: every action settles inside one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114) and core reads no block field, so a dropped block takes its whole PoolManager effect with it.
findings.impact: No loss of pool funds and no locked funds. An off-chain integration that credits a user on a latest receipt of a PoolManager take could pay out for a swap that never finalizes. On the sample taken no block served at latest was replaced.
findings.preconditions: A Monad leader that equivocates or a proposal that misses its vote, and an integration that acts on latest. An ordinary account cannot make a proposal miss its vote with a transaction.
findings.mitigations: Integrations and bridges on Monad should settle on finalized, which lags latest by one to two blocks (about 0.4 to 0.8 s), or compare the receipt block number with the finalized height as the Monad documentation advises.

sources.supports: latest maps to Proposed with no consensus vote, safe to Voted, finalized to Finalized; transaction-hash lookups can match a transaction in a non-finalized block
a Proposed block may never be Voted; finalizing a number implicitly abandons other proposals at that number
v0.13.0 moved latest from Finalized to Proposed (monad-bft PR 2675)

get_latest_block_key returns the latest proposed block key (lines 91-93); Latest and Safe tags resolve to proposed and voted keys (102-106); receipts are looked up against the latest proposed key (196-225)
Latest is commented proposed, Safe voted, pending parses to Latest (lines 328-330, 373-376)

findings.title: From T14 Tempo validators vote to notarize a block before its execution is verified and withhold only the finalize vote
findings.difference: Tempo v1.19.0 and v1.19.1 default --consensus.verification-mode to hardfork, which switches to deferred verification at the first epoch boundary at or after T14 (8 December 2026 15:00 UTC, timestamp 1796742000). Under deferred verification a validator checks only that the block is available, that its embedded consensus context matches and that it names the expected parent before it votes to notarize. The execution check (newPayload VALID) runs while the vote collects and gates the finalize vote.
findings.mechanism: crates/consensus/src/args.rs:35-56 and 153-165 define the modes; crates/consensus/src/consensus/application/mod.rs:120-143 selects the Deferred wrapper of commonware-consensus 2026.11.0, whose module documentation (marshal/standard/deferred.rs:15-37) says the notarize vote is cast without waiting for the application to verify the block contents, and certify waits for that result before a finalize vote. If certify returns false the validator broadcasts nullify for the view and refuses to build on the block (simplex/mod.rs:106-111, 138-140), so a block whose execution is wrong cannot gather a finalization from an honest quorum and is never finalized. Nothing in the source read slashes the proposer. The executor of an RPC node moves HEAD to a notarized convergence target only after its own newPayload returned VALID and its ancestry reaches the network finalized tip; otherwise HEAD is the finalized block, and safe and finalized are always the finalized block (crates/consensus/src/executor/actor.rs:12-25 and 2884-2889). A wallet reading latest on such a node therefore reads a block the node itself executed correctly, which a nullified view can still replace. The PoolManager settles inside one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), so no PoolManager state outlives the replaced block.
findings.impact: No loss of pool funds. After T14 an integration acting on latest can, in a view that is notarized and then nullified, see a PoolManager take that does not reach the final chain. A wrong arithmetic result in one validator's build cannot be finalized unless a quorum shares it, as before T14.
findings.preconditions: Tempo T14 active, a validator set that notarizes and then nullifies a view, and an integration that acts on latest. Only validators act.
findings.mitigations: Integrations on Tempo should read finalized (equal to safe) after T14. A day-one sample of latest against finalized should confirm whether the public endpoint moves HEAD past finalized.

sources.supports: VerificationMode Immediate completes application verification before voting to notarize, Deferred defers it until voting to finalize, Hardfork follows T14 (lines 35-56, 153-165)
the factory hands each epoch the Deferred or Inline marshal wrapper by the previous epoch boundary timestamp (lines 1-12, 120-143)
notarize vote without waiting for application verification; certify gates the finalize vote; certify false leads to nullify and no child built on the block
HEAD becomes a notarized convergence target only after the node's own newPayload VALID; safe and finalized hashes are the finalized block (lines 12-25, 2884-2889)
v1.19.0 is required for T14 at 1796742000 and the verification mode defaults to hardfork
the consensus context in the header exists for deferred verification, and a validator may keep synchronous verification

cleared.check: Task 3: does Arc's consensus vote before the execution result is checked, in arc-node main and in what v0.9.0 announces, and what each tag resolves to on rpc.mainnet.arc.io and arc.drpc.org.
cleared.result: In arc-node main a validator that receives a full proposal calls the engine newPayload and sets the block validity from the VALID or INVALID answer before it hands the proposed value to Malachite (crates/malachite-app/src/handlers/received_proposal_part.rs:368-410, crates/malachite-app/src/payload.rs:234-307 and 319-361), so execution is checked before the prevote. The decided block is made canonical by forkchoiceUpdated after the decision (crates/malachite-app/src/finalize.rs:89-119), and the IPC engine sets head, safe and finalized to the same hash (crates/eth-engine/src/ipc/engine_ipc.rs:98-109). v0.9.0 is announced only as the removal of the HTTP transport between the two layers in favour of IPC (CHANGELOG v0.8.0, docs.arc.io run-an-arc-node); nothing announced changes when execution is checked. On chain latest, safe and finalized were equal in every snapshot on both endpoints and 700 blocks read at latest kept their hash. The endpoints run unpublished commits (arc/v1), so the reading applies to the public branch.

cleared.check: Task 1, L-1106: which Tempo validators run binaries built with the jit feature, and the LLVM stage rules for MULMOD, ADDMOD, SAR, SHL, SIGNEXTEND and JUMPI.
cleared.result: jit is an optional feature of bin/tempo (bin/tempo/Cargo.toml:267-268) outside the default set (line 155: asm-keccak, jemalloc, otlp, keccak-cache-global). The release workflow builds the tempo binary with features asm-keccak,jemalloc,otlp on x86_64 and arm64 (.github/workflows/release.yml:127-131, 176) and the Dockerfile uses the same list (line 7). No release note, operator page or build file found in this session says any validator builds with jit; the v1.19.0 notes list no such option. Tempo validators are permissioned, so a jit build is an operator choice. The LLVM stage rules for these opcodes at Tempo v1.19.1 were transcribed and checked in an earlier cycle (OPCODES.md, reth compiler row: arithmetic opcodes call the interpreter's integer routines; SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, shifts, comparisons and JUMPI inline code checked on 631,353 vectors) and evm2 is at the same revision 35aa3280 in a9d6748 (Cargo.toml:324, 460), so that result stands. Under deferred verification a validator with a wrong result still cannot finalize a block alone.

cleared.check: L-1100: with --builder.parallel or the T15 test is_payment_v3, can a replayed action reach a contract other than a TIP-20 token or the channel reserve, for example a TIP-20 transfer to the PoolManager followed by settle.
cleared.result: A transaction is a replay candidate only if it is a payment (is_payment_v2 today, is_payment_v3 after T15) and uses a nonzero 2D or expiring nonce (crates/payload/builder/src/prewarming.rs:497-506). Both payment rules require every call to target a TIP-20 address (0x20c0 prefix) with a recognised payment selector or the channel reserve, and forbid access lists and authorization lists (crates/primitives/src/transaction/envelope.rs:282-330, 622-637); v3 only adds trailing bytes and voucher signatures. A TIP-20 transfer whose recipient is the PoolManager is a candidate, but a TIP-20 transfer is a precompile write and runs no code at the recipient, so no PoolManager code runs in the replay. The PoolManager's settle in the next transaction is not a payment and always runs serially (crates/payload/builder/src/lib.rs:653-668), reading the token balance the replay wrote. A replay that no longer applies is skipped as invalid_replay (lib.rs:713-731). Replay exists only in the block builder; other validators execute the block through newPayload, so a replay that diverged from serial execution gives a state root they reject and the block is not finalized. Parallel building is off unless the operator enables it (lib.rs:153-154).

cleared.check: Task 5: does anything in src/ depend on finality, including ERC-6909 claims and protocol fee accrual.
cleared.result: No. unlock opens the lock, runs the callback and reverts unless the nonzero delta count is zero before it locks again (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114); take, settle, settleFor, clear, mint and burn all require the lock and only move transient deltas besides the transfer or claim write (src/PoolManager.sol:291-336, 349-364). The lock, deltas, delta count and synced reserves live in transient storage (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32), so nothing carries between transactions. sync may run without the lock but only writes transient storage (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). ERC-6909 transfer, transferFrom, approve and setOperator are plain storage writes (src/ERC6909.sol:25-64). Protocol fees accrue in persistent storage within the same swap transaction (src/ProtocolFees.sol:66-70) and are withdrawn only by the controller (lines 44-57). No file in src/ outside src/test reads block.number, block.timestamp, blockhash, tx.origin or any other block field (search of src/). A replaced block removes every PoolManager effect of its transactions together, so core has no state that a later block can see half applied.

cleared.check: Task 1: what happens to a notarized block whose execution turns out wrong under T14.
cleared.result: It is not finalized. A validator whose certify returns false broadcasts nullify for that view and does not build on the block; a finalization needs a quorum of certify results (commonware-consensus 2026.11.0 simplex/mod.rs:106-111, 138-140). The chain does not halt on one bad block: the view is nullified and the next leader proposes on a certified parent. Validators that cannot complete verification withhold their finalize vote and count as faulty for that view (marshal/standard/deferred.rs:33-37). No slashing of the proposer was found in the files read. The executor treats an INVALID answer as the verdict and caches it (crates/consensus/src/executor/actor.rs:64-80).

leads.question: After T14 activates on 8 December 2026 15:00 UTC (timestamp 1796742000), does rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz serve latest ahead of finalized, and does any block served at latest fail to finalize? Rerun scripts/monad_heads.py against the endpoint for 2,000 heads.
leads.why: The executor may move HEAD to a notarized block under deferred verification; today latest equals finalized, so the post-T14 behaviour has not been observed.

leadResults.answer: Release binaries and the Dockerfile are built without jit; no operator page or release note says any Tempo validator runs a jit build. The LLVM stage rules at the same evm2 revision were checked in an earlier cycle. T14 defers execution verification to the finalize vote, so a validator with a wrong result still cannot finalize a block alone (new finding on deferred verification, info).

arc-node main executes the proposed payload through newPayload before the vote and sets head, safe and finalized to the decided block. v0.9.0 only removes the HTTP transport. Both endpoints served latest equal to finalized.

Replay candidates must call only TIP-20 tokens or the channel reserve under both v2 and v3 rules; a TIP-20 transfer to the PoolManager runs no PoolManager code, settle runs serially, and validators re-execute the block.

latest on rpc.monad.xyz is the Proposed block, with no vote, for eth_call, eth_getBalance and receipts; 2,000 heads and 70 PoolManager receipts read at latest all finalized unchanged; recorded as an operator-level low finding.
